note: Attacker-controlled bytes are wrapped in a synthetic reader and become the input source for the PKCS#15 reader path.
The first two attacker bytes determine the length of the next chunk, so later parsing decisions are fully input-driven.
The synthetic reader is connected to OpenSC, causing the Coolkey card driver to initialize card state from the fuzzed APDU stream.
During card teardown, the driver frees the private Coolkey state, including per-object payload buffers stored in the object list.
Each object's data buffer is released here; if the same object list is later torn down again, the same heap pointer is freed twice.
The PKCS#15 wrapper is freed after the driver teardown path has already run, triggering a second cleanup of the same Coolkey private data and reaching the double-free sink.
